description: Single-panel line plot (V-bending spring-back comparison) with a frame and horizontal gridlines. The y-axis is labelled "Springback [degree]", spanning 0 to 1.6 with gridlines every 0.2. The x-axis is labelled "Bend angle before unloading [degree]" and is drawn in reverse order, running from 180 on the left to 80 on the right with ticks every 10 degrees. A framed legend in the lower-right corner lists three series with their marker symbols: "experimental" (diamond), "Simulated with constant E" (square) and "Simulated with varied E" (triangle). Markers are placed at bend angles of 160, 140, 120, 100 and 90 degrees. All three series show springback increasing as the bend angle decreases from 160 to 90 degrees. The diamond-marked experimental curve rises from a little above the 0.8 gridline to the highest point, just under 1.4. The triangle-marked "Simulated with varied E" curve follows the experimental points closely across the whole range. The square-marked "Simulated with constant E" curve is the lowest and flattest, rising only from about the 1.0 gridline to about the 1.2 gridline, and its gap to the experimental curve widens as bend angle decreases. The figure demonstrates that a strain-dependent (varied) elastic modulus predicts measured spring-back far more accurately than a constant initial modulus.

subfigures.description: Line plot of springback (degree, 0-1.6) versus bend angle before unloading (degree, reversed axis 180 to 80). Three marker series: experimental (diamonds), Simulated with constant E (squares) and Simulated with varied E (triangles), sampled at 160, 140, 120, 100 and 90 degrees bend angle. Springback rises as bend angle decreases; the varied-E simulation tracks the experimental points closely while the constant-E simulation lies lowest.

observations.observation: The y-axis is labelled "Springback [degree]" and is scaled 0 to 1.6 with horizontal gridlines at 0.2 intervals.
The x-axis is labelled "Bend angle before unloading [degree]" and is plotted in reverse order, from 180 at the left edge to 80 at the right edge, with a tick every 10 degrees.
The legend contains exactly three entries with distinct marker symbols: "experimental" (diamond), "Simulated with constant E" (square) and "Simulated with varied E" (triangle).
Data markers are plotted at bend angles of 160, 140, 120, 100 and 90 degrees.
All three curves show springback increasing monotonically as the bend angle before unloading decreases from 160 to 90 degrees.
The diamond-marked experimental curve reaches its highest value just below the 1.4 gridline at a bend angle of 90 degrees and its lowest value a little above the 0.8 gridline at 160 degrees.
The square-marked "Simulated with constant E" curve is the lowest of the three and the flattest, remaining between roughly the 1.0 and 1.2 gridlines over the whole bend-angle range.

The triangle-marked "Simulated with varied E" curve stays close to the experimental diamonds at every plotted bend angle, whereas the constant-E squares fall progressively further below the experimental values as the bend angle decreases.
The figure caption identifies the plot as "Comparison of experimental and simulated spring-back value in the V-bending test".
The citing text states that the varied elastic modulus was defined from the experimental results shown in Fig. 1 [4].
The citing text asserts that spring-back predicted with the varied elastic modulus is more accurate than that predicted with the constant initial elastic modulus.
No numerical data labels are printed on the data points; values must be read against the 0.2-degree y-gridlines.
